# `billing_export` — version 1.0

Source: `presets/billing-export.satz`

## Purpose

Cloud Billing usage and cost data, exported to BigQuery in a project of its own —
where the spend is KEPT, as opposed to the budget that alarms on it.

A budget (`presets/organization-budget.satz`) says when a threshold is crossed; this
says what the money went on, per project, per SKU, per day, queryable months later.

ITS OWN PROJECT. The export is not infrastructure and its dataset is read by whoever
reviews spend, so it lives in a project of its own rather than in the infrastructure
project: reading the billing dataset then never means reading the state bucket beside
it. The project takes the same billing account as the infrastructure project and
carries one API, BigQuery's.

SWITCHING THE EXPORT ON IS A CONSOLE STEP. Cloud Billing has no API, no gcloud command
and no Terraform resource for pointing a billing account at a dataset. This pack
builds everything the console asks for — the project, the dataset, and the export
account's access to it — and the `notice` below names the step and the param that
acknowledges it. Until it is done the dataset stays empty.

THE EXPORT ACCOUNT. Google writes the export as
`billing-export-bigquery@system.gserviceaccount.com`, a Google-owned account in a
Google-owned domain, the same for every customer. Two things follow, and this pack
does both: it holds `roles/bigquery.dataEditor` on the dataset, and — because it lives
outside the customer's organisation — it is CONTRIBUTED to the CIS baseline's
`allowed_policy_member_subjects`, so domain-restricted sharing lets the grant through.
Switch this pack off and the entry goes with it.

NO CLAIM. No catalog control covers billing export, so this pack witnesses nothing.

## Use it

```
params {
  use_billing_export = true

  // the pack's own defaults — copy only the lines you change
  billing_export_project_id = "{customer_shortname}-billing-001"
  billing_export_project_folder = ""
  billing_export_project_display_name = billing_export_project_id
  billing_export_dataset_id = "{customer_shortname}_billing_export"
  billing_export_location = default_region
  billing_export_description = "Cloud Billing usage and cost data, exported continuously"
}

use "presets/billing-export.satz" when use_billing_export
```

`use_billing_export` is the gate: while it is falsy the pack contributes nothing — no resources, no params, no claims. It is declared by `estate_map`, and the estate's own binding wins.

**Needs from outside the pack:**

- `allowed_policy_member_subjects` — declared by `CIS_GCP_Foundation_4_0`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `billing_account_infra` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `customer_shortname` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.
- `default_region` — declared by `estate_core`; use one of them alongside, or declare it in the estate.

## Questions

What to ask before this pack is configured, and what changing the answer costs.

| asks about | prompt | reversal | blast | recommends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `billing_export_project_id` | The project that holds the billing export | recreate | high | — |
| `billing_export_project_folder` | The folder the billing-export project is created in — a folder the estate declares as `google_folder.<label>.name`, an existing one by its numeric id, or empty for the organisation | edit | low | — |
| `billing_export_dataset_id` | The dataset the billing export writes into | recreate | high | — |
| `billing_export_location` | Where the billing dataset lives (a BigQuery location, e.g. europe-west3 or EU) | recreate | high | — |

**billing_export_project_id** — A project id is immutable. Changing it later creates a second project and abandons the first, with the billing history inside it — and the console export has to be pointed at the new dataset by hand.


**billing_export_project_folder** — It is the only thing that decides where the project lands. Left empty, the project is created directly under the organisation and inherits the organisation's policies and IAM alone. Changing it afterwards moves a live project between parents, which changes the policies and the grants it inherits.


**billing_export_dataset_id** — Whoever can read it reads what every project in the organisation costs. A dataset id cannot be renamed: a new one is a new dataset the console export has to be pointed at, and the history stays in the old one.


**billing_export_location** — A dataset's location cannot change: moving it means a new dataset and no history. Where the CIS pack enforces allowed resource locations, a location outside that list is refused. The default follows the estate's own default region.


## Notices

What to run once this pack is switched on. satz shows each notice when the pack goes on and until the estate binds its param `true`; every command that writes to the organisation refuses while one whose severity is `error` is open.

| param | run | severity | what and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `billing_export_enabled` | `https://console.cloud.google.com/billing — the billing account, Billing export, BigQuery export, Edit settings` | warning | Cloud Billing has no API, no gcloud command and no Terraform resource for switching the export on. Apply this pack first, then in the Cloud console open Billing, pick the billing account, go to Billing export, BigQuery export, and point Standard usage cost at the project `billing_export_project_id` names and the dataset `billing_export_dataset_id` names. The dataset stays empty until that is done. Bind this param true once it is. |
